original.context: The proposed first-order test requires a distinct comparison state phi satisfying supp Lambda_x^c(phi) subset supp Lambda_x^c(psi). It treats this as a three-dimensional domain from which random kernel-avoiding pairs can be drawn.

witness.explanation: The environment-support restriction can force phi=|psi><psi|, so the assumed nontrivial comparison domain does not exist.
witness.evidence: For psi=|0> and 0<x<1, use Kraus operators K0=sqrt(1-x)I and K_(mu+1)=sqrt(x/2)A_mu, (A_mu)_(jk)=epsilon_(mu j k). The complementary output has kernel vector z=(0,1,0,0). Positivity and support inclusion imply Tr(K1 phi K1^dagger)=0, hence supp(phi) subset ker K1=span{|0>}. Since phi has trace one it equals |0><0|. The claimed random distinct-pair construction therefore fails already in this exact instance; generic tests in the recorded check also had one-dimensional allowed support.
